categories.main_business_segments: Air Lease Corporation operates as a single business segment focused on the acquisition, leasing, and sale of modern, fuel-efficient commercial jet aircraft. The company also provides fleet management services to third-party investors and owners of aircraft portfolios for a management fee.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: ALC's core operations involve purchasing new technology aircraft directly from major manufacturers such as Airbus and Boeing, often customizing aircraft with buyer-furnished equipment to meet customer specifications. The company leverages deep industry relationships and market analysis to select in-demand, fuel-efficient aircraft, and utilizes structured operating leases with airlines globally.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are commercial airlines worldwide, ranging from major carriers in mature markets (such as the U.S. and Western Europe) focused on fleet replacement, to rapidly growing airlines in emerging markets seeking fleet expansion. As of December 31, 2024, ALC had 116 airline customers in 58 countries, with no single airline or country representing more than 10% of rental revenue.
categories.geographic_coverage: ALC operates globally, with over 95% of its aircraft placed internationally. The largest regions by fleet net book value are Europe (41.4%) and Asia Pacific (35.8%), followed by Central and South America, the Middle East and Africa, and North America. The customer base is highly diversified across these regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: ALC is positioned downstream in the aviation supply chain, acting as an intermediary between aircraft manufacturers (upstream) and airline operators (end users). The company does not manufacture or operate aircraft but owns, leases, and manages aircraft assets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, ALC focuses on maintaining a young, modern, and fuel-efficient fleet to meet airline demand for lower emissions and operating costs. The company prioritizes direct orders of new aircraft, fleet diversification, risk management, and capital efficiency. Sustainability and supporting airline fleet modernization are key themes, with ongoing attention to supply chain challenges and delivery delays.
categories.revenue_model: ALC generates revenue primarily through long-term operating leases of aircraft to airlines, which are typically structured as triple-net leases with fixed payments in U.S. dollars. Additional revenue streams include gains from aircraft sales and trading, as well as management fees from third-party fleet management services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: ALC is one of the largest global aircraft lessors, competing with other major leasing companies, banks, financial institutions, and, to a lesser extent, aircraft manufacturers and airlines. The industry is highly competitive, with competition based on lease rates, aircraft availability, terms, and customer relationships. Some competitors may have greater resources or lower capital costs.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2024, ALC owned 489 aircraft with a net book value of $28.2 billion and managed 60 additional aircraft. Total revenues for 2024 were $2.7 billion, up 1.8% year-over-year, with net income attributable to common stockholders of $372.1 million. The fleet and revenue base have grown steadily, though 2024 net income declined due to higher interest expenses.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: ALC differentiates itself by offering airlines access to one of the youngest, most modern, and fuel-efficient fleets, enabling customers to reduce fuel costs, emissions, and noise. The company emphasizes global reach, deep industry expertise, flexible lease structures, and the ability to deliver customized aircraft configurations, supporting airlines' fleet modernization and operational flexibility.
